construction-materials.features:

• High thixotropy allows overhead and vertical placement up to 50 mm without slumping
• Exceptional adhesion to properly prepared parent concrete and primed rebar
• Extremely low permeability protects internal rebar against carbonation and chloride ingress

construction-materials.appSchedule: Complete Structural Concrete Restoration System: Defect removal ➔ Rebar protection ➔ Polymer bonding slurry ➔ High-build Patchfix placement ➔ Curing membrane ➔ Architectural skimcoat. Stage 1 - Preparation: 1. Chipping & Saw Cutting: Saw cut repair perimeter edges to minimum 10 mm depth to prevent feather edging. Chip away all spalled or carbonated concrete. 2. Rebar Cleaning: Expose corroded rebar 20 mm all around; wire-brush to Sa 2.5 and apply zinc-rich anti-corrosion primer. 3. Water Stopping (if active seepage): Plug active running water immediately using before mortar application. 4. Bonding Slurry: Pre-soak concrete to Saturated Surface Dry (SSD) condition. Scrub an active bonding slurry of mixed 1:1 with fresh Portland cement into substrate. Stage 2 - Main Work: 1. Water Ratio: Measure 3.5 – 3.8 Liters clean potable water per 25 kg bag. Pour 80% water into drum, add Patchfix powder gradually while running low-speed mixer (400-500 rpm) for 3 minutes, then add remaining water to desired consistency. 2. Application: Press mortar firmly into repair cavity wet-on-wet over tacky SBR slurry using steel trowel, eliminating all air pockets. 3. Layer Build: Can be applied up to 50 mm in a single vertical pass. For deeper voids (>50 mm), build up in successive layers, scoring intermediate surfaces. Stage 3 - Detailing: 1. Trowel Finishing: Finish flush with surrounding parent concrete using wooden float or steel trowel. 2. Do NOT feather-edge repair edges; maintain clean 10 mm square shoulder. Stage 4 - Finishing & Curing: 1. Curing: Prevent rapid evaporation by spraying non-degrading curing compound immediately after final troweling (or wet cure with damp burlap for 3 days). 2. Architectural Finishing: Once cured (minimum 24-48 hrs), smooth wall surface with before applying decorative paint.
construction-materials.surfacePrep: Saw cut repair perimeter edges to minimum 10 mm depth to prevent feather edging. Chip away all deteriorated, cracked, or carbonated concrete until sound substrate is reached. Clean all grease, oil, dust, and contaminants. Thoroughly saturate surface with clean water 2-4 hours prior to placement, blowing off standing water before application.
construction-materials.materialPrep: Always use whole bags. Store indoors on pallets away from damp floors. Do not retemper stiffened mortar with water.

construction-materials.appSchedule: Precision Machinery & Baseplate Grouting System: Surface scabbling ➔ Formwork water-tight sealing ➔ Continuous non-shrink grouting ➔ Moisture curing. Stage 1 - Preparation: 1. Concrete Foundation Scabbling: Chisel or grit-blast foundation to expose sound aggregate. Clear all dust and grease. 2. Water Pre-Soaking: Saturate concrete base with clean water for 24 hours prior to grouting (SSD condition); blow out water from bolt pockets. 3. Formwork Sealing: Erect rigid formwork with a 45° headbox (100-150 mm head). Seal all formwork joints water-tight using or to prevent grout slurry leakage. Stage 2 - Main Work: 1. Water Ratio: Measure 4.0 – 4.3 Liters water per 25 kg bag for flowable consistency (3.5 – 3.8 L for pourable). Mix mechanically with pan mixer for 4 minutes. 2. Continuous Pour: Pour grout continuously from one side only to displace air and prevent voids. 3. Minimum Clearance: Maintain minimum 25 mm gap under baseplates for flowable consistency. Stage 3 - Detailing: 1. Shoulder Trimming: Once grout reaches initial set (stiff putty consistency), trim exposed shoulders flush or at 45° chamfer with steel trowel. Stage 4 - Finishing & Curing: 1. Curing: Retain formwork for 24 hours. Immediately spray onto exposed grout shoulders or keep continuously wet with damp burlap for 3 days. 2. Torquing: Final machine bolt tightening can proceed after 72 hours (>40 MPa).

1. Dovetail Chipping: Chisel crack or hole to minimum 25 mm depth and 25 mm width, undercutting edges into a dovetail shape (NEVER cut a V-shape, as water pressure will blow plug out).
2. Flushing: Flush out all loose stone chips and debris.
structuredSchedule.mainStage:
1. Quick Mix: Measure 1 part clean water to 4 parts Powerplug powder by volume. Mix rapidly by hand (wearing heavy rubber gloves) for 20-30 seconds into stiff putty.
2. Conical Shaping: Shape mortar into a cone as it begins to warm and stiffen.
3. Direct Insertion: Force the conical plug aggressively into the center of the water leak with palm.
4. Pressure Hold: Maintain heavy palm pressure against water flow for 90 to 120 seconds until rock hard.
structuredSchedule.detailStage: 1. Trimming: Scrape excess flush with surrounding wall after 3 minutes.
structuredSchedule.finishStage: 1. Secondary Waterproofing: After leak is stopped, coat surrounding concrete with or to prevent water bypassing into adjacent capillaries.

waterproofing.title: Bostik Superswell
waterproofing.subtitle: Hydrophilic Swellable Waterstop for Concrete Construction Joints
waterproofing.desc: Bostik Superswell is a high-performance hydrophilic butyl bentonite swellable waterstop strip designed to seal non-moving construction joints, pipe penetrations, and precast concrete joints against water penetration by expanding up to 300% upon contact with water.
waterproofing.highlight: Hydrophilic Swellable Waterstop • Expands Up to 300% • Withstands >5 Bar Hydrostatic Pressure
waterproofing.packaging: 20 mm x 25 mm strip (5 meters per roll, 30 m per box) or 20 mm x 10 mm
waterproofing.yieldCoverage: Direct linear measurement (1 meter of joint = 1 meter of Superswell)
waterproofing.potLifeCure: Controlled expansion begins within 24-48 hours of water immersion

techData.chemicalBase: High-grade sodium bentonite and hydrophilic synthetic butyl rubber polymer matrix
techData.compressiveStrength: Hydrostatic Head Resistance: >50 meters (>5 bar) | Swelling Capacity: >300% free swell
techData.coverage: 1 meter strip per linear meter of joint
techData.applicationMethod: Adhered along center of joint using Bostik Seal 'N' Flex or concrete masonry nails
techData.thinning: Solid pre-formed strip
techData.uses: Construction cold joints in basement foundation slabs, retaining walls, swimming pool shells, pipe penetrations, box culverts.

waterproofing.features:
• Controlled delayed expansion prevents premature swelling during initial concrete curing
• Conforms to irregular concrete profiles to seal micro-fissures and aggregate gaps
• Repeated expansion and contraction capability across wet-dry weather cycles
• Simple, fast installation without requiring specialized split-forming
